label: Person
name: Adam Exner
summary:
Adam Exner (1928–2014) was a Canadian bishop of German-Ukrainian descent who served as Archbishop of Vancouver, making him one of the most prominent Catholic leaders in western Canada. Born in Saskatchewan to Ukrainian immigrant parents, he was ordained a priest of the Oblates of Mary Immaculate and served in the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church before his appointment to Latin Rite leadership.

Exner was appointed Bishop of Kamloops in 1974 and Archbishop of Winnipeg in 1982 before being transferred to the Archdiocese of Vancouver in 1991, a position he held until 2004. His episcopate in Vancouver coincided with the city's dramatic transformation into one of Canada's most diverse and socially complex metropolises. He navigated controversies including the clergy sex abuse crisis, debates over Catholic hospital mergers, and the Church's engagement with Canada's increasingly multicultural and secular society.

As a Ukrainian Canadian, Exner brought a distinctive sensitivity to Eastern Christian traditions and the immigrant Catholic experience in western Canada. He was known for his direct pastoral style and his willingness to engage public debate, including on bioethical questions where Catholic hospitals' policies were contested. His tenure shaped the Vancouver Archdiocese at a formative moment of its history.
